pool.text: The University of Nantes, the first in Brittany, was founded.
Rennes became the provincial capital after the union of Brittany and France.
The Edict of Nantes legalising Protestantism in France was signed.
Nantes shipowners began trading African slaves in the colonies.
Locals seized the Castle of the Dukes of Brittany.
A rum cake was invented in Nantes and became a popular local specialty.
The city was captured by Nazi Germany during the Battle.
Forty-eight civilians were executed in retaliation for an assassination.
The Germans abandoned the city and it was recaptured.
Samuel Boggs identified the geographical centre near the station.
Metallurgists organised a strike protesting salary disparities with Paris.
Port activity in Saint-Nazaire ceased, culminating in shipyard closures.
Nantes Metropole was created and administered by a council.
The city developed a business district named Euronantes.
Télénantes, a local private television channel, was established in the city.
The city adopted an ecological framework to reduce greenhouse gases.
The Voyage à Nantes contemporary art summer exhibition series began across the city.
Nantes received the prestigious European Green Capital Award.
Johanna Rolland was elected as the current mayor.
The annual festival sold a record number of tickets in this year.
